subject: Montara — post-call technical recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Duarte <alex.duarte@montara.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@montara.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-24T18:05:00Z
Subject: Montara — post-call technical recap & next steps

Alex / Priya — thanks again for taking the deep-dive with us today. Short recap below from our side and a proposed next-play to keep momentum going. Please correct anything I get wrong.

TL;DR: Montara is evaluating Redwood to serve low-latency LLM inference for two product surfaces: (1) real-time assistant (customer-facing chat) with a firm p95 latency target, and (2) batch document summarization for overnight processing. Key constraints: strict P95 <= 250ms for live paths, 1–2M tokens/day baseline, and HIPAA-adjacent controls for metadata retention.

What we heard (pain & goals)
- Live assistant: current in-house model has ~400ms p95 at 512-token prompts; customer wants sub-250ms p95 for 95% of queries, spikes allowed with fallback to cheaper model.
- Throughput: expectation of steady 40 RPS on peak and burst to 150 RPS during marketing spikes.
- Model quality: want an open LLM (prefer smaller context-optimized variant) that retains generation fidelity for task-specific prompts (customer-provided prompt set).
- Security/compliance: logs must be retained for 90 days, encryption-at-rest, and VPC peering for private deployment.

Immediate asks we committed to
1) Deliver a short topology sketch + latency test plan (attached: montara-architecture-sketch.pdf; redwood-latency-test-plan.xlsx).
2) Provide expected unit economics and recommended model variants for live assistant (vCPU/GPU sizing, quantization tradeoffs).
3) Arrange a SRE + model engineer follow-up next week to validate socket-level time-to-first-token expectations.

Proposed next steps (owners & timing)
- Today: share topology sketch & test plan (attached) — Marissa (done).
- Tue 2028-07-26: deep SRE sync (Karthik + Montara infra) — action: map burst provisioning and KV cache sizing.
- Fri 2028-08-02: deliver latency microbench (90/95/99 percentiles) using Montara prompt set on Redwood hosted dev cluster — owner: Karthik.

Question for you: can you confirm whether data residency must remain in us-east-1, and whether we should include an on-prem option in the readout?

Attachments: montara-architecture-sketch.pdf (PDF), redwood-latency-test-plan.xlsx (XLSX)

Thanks — talk soon.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Marissa — huge thanks for the summary. High-level: this aligns well. Couple of clarifications and one ask.

Clarifications
- The p95 target is for interactive UI flows (customer-facing). For webhooks/back-office async workers we can tolerate higher latency (p95 <= 1s).
- Throughput: the 40 RPS steady-state is per-region; plan will be multi-region (us-east-1 primary, us-west-2 DR).

One ask
- Can the latency microbench include cold-start (first request after a scale-to-zero) and KV cache warm/cold scenarios? Those have been the biggest delta for us.

Also attaching a quick note on compliance: we will need a short statement of Redwood's approach to audit logs and KMS integration for the procurement team. No need to be legal-language perfect — a 1-paragraph technical summary will do.

On dates: Tue 2028-07-26 for the SRE sync works for our infra lead Priya. I can share sample prompts before the bench run.

Thanks — Alex

Date: 2028-07-25T08:20:00Z
Subject: Montara — SLO/Topology draft + internal asks (please review)

Team — looping you both in with the updated asks from Montara. Alex confirmed multi-region intent and the cold-start/KV-cache scenarios. Below is a more technical readout we should validate before the Tue SRE sync.

SLO targets (customer-facing live assistant)- p95 latency <= 250ms for 512-token requests (target context window 512 tokens).- p99 latency <= 500ms for same profile (allowable but will impact product UX).- sustained throughput baseline: 40 RPS per region, burst to 150 RPS (2 min bucket)

Model & runtime constraints- Preferred models: open Llama2-style family or equivalent (Montara wants an open checkpoint). Provide 3 variants: 1) high-quality 70B (quantized), 2) mid-size 13–20B (recommended primary), 3) small 7B for fallback.- Quantization: int8 / 4-bit feasible for 13–20B to hit latency targets w/ negligible quality loss on prompt set — include A/B bench notes.

Topology recommendations- Hosted Redwood (multi-tenant) for dev/benching; Dedicated pool (reserved GPUs) for production live assistant.- Multi-region routing: primary us-east-1 with regional fallback to us-west-2; use smart routing policy by latency with automatic fallback to mid-size model if p95 rises > 300ms.- KV / prefix caching: prefix caching at edge + regional KV cache (Redis) with an LRU TTL of 2 hours; plan to warm cache during marketing event windows.

Autoscaling & burst plan- Slow-start policy: maintain a small warm pool to reduce cold-start frequency.- Burst provisioning: ephemeral burst nodes that can be added within 30s; we suggested a warm fraction sized for 10% of expected peak and a fast scale path for the remainder.

Security/compliance notes- VPC peering and Private deployment option recommended for HIPAA-adjacent controls.- KMS integration for model encryption keys; 90-day audit-log retention requirement captured.

Bench plan for Tue run (owner: Karthik)- Microbench scenarios: cold-start, warm-KV, warm-with-prefix-cache, burst-load ramp to 150 RPS.- Metrics: TTF (time-to-first-token), p50/p95/p99 latency, CPU/GPU utilization, KV hit rate.

Immediate internal asks- Karthik: validate whether 13–20B quantized on A100-nv4 at 40 RPS p95 <= 250ms is realistic with the current kernels; add any kernel/compilation caveats.- Vivek: confirm pricing guidance for Dedicated pool + burst nodes so I can include in the commercial note to Montara.- Marissa: I will draft the 1-paragraph compliance summary for procurement and circulate for review.

Proposed shared M.A.P. (mutual action plan) milestones
- 2028-07-26: SRE sync (technical bench inputs) — owner: Karthik.- 2028-08-02: deliver bench readout + economics — owner: Karthik & Vivek.- 2028-08-09: procurement redlines + security checklist — owner: Alex / Montara procurement.

Please add comments inline on the Drive link if you see misalignment: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-montara-arch

Thanks — will finalize before Tue and share a single slide for the customer meeting.
